messages:
Ava: Heads-up — turned up a pattern in prod: ~30% of requests to /generate still come in wrapped in the legacy envelope shape (e.g. {"input": ..., "meta": ...}). Runtime v5 wants to drop envelope parsing at the gateway to simplify streaming and reduce memory copies. We need a safe rollout plan and a lightweight edge shim so customers don't break.

Ken: Can we avoid parsing body at the edge entirely? header-detection seems cheaper.

Sam: +1 to header detection. Some tenants send X-Runtime-Version but not all.

Maria: Confirmed — mobile SDKs frequently omit custom headers, so relying only on headers will miss a chunk of traffic.

Jordan: Proposal: deploy a very small Envoy/Lua filter that inspects up to the first 4KB of body, attempts a safe JSON decode, and rewrites the request to the new shape (move envelope.input -> body). If parse fails or exceeds limits, forward unchanged and increment a compat counter.

Olivia: Parsing JSON at the edge raises CPU and DoS concerns. We must enforce size/time caps, and guardrails for abusive tenants.

Ava: Agreed. Constraints to enforce: inspect only prefix (4KB), max CPU budget ~2ms per req on the filter, and a global rate limit per tenant for shim path. Also require strict content-length checks and early reject for absurd sizes.

Sam: Telemetry plan: emit metrics compat_shim_hit, compat_shim_latency_ms, compat_shim_parse_fail, compat_shim_forwarded_without_change. Tag by tenant_id and route. Add alert if parse_fail_ratio > 5% for >5m.

Jordan: Minimal safe Lua sketch (prototype):
```lua
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local max = 4096
  local body = request_handle:body():getBytes(0, max)
  if not body then return end
  local ok, obj = pcall(function() return cjson.decode(body) end)
  if ok and obj and obj.input then
    -- rewrite to new body shape (danger: keep this minimal)
    request_handle:headers():replace('content-type', 'application/json')
    request_handle:body():setBytes(cjson.encode(obj.input))
    -- attach a small dynamic metadata flag for tracing
    request_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():set('compat','shim','hit')
  else
    -- increment parse_fail counter via stats extension (implementation detail)
  end
end
```

Maria: Works for single-chunk requests. Chunked streaming is harder — we won't attempt to rewrite streaming bodies. The filter should be disabled for chunked transfer-encoding / streaming endpoints.

Ken: Policy question: do we opt-in tenants, or do we flip-on globally and watch?

Ava: Rollout suggestion: 1) Canary the filter in staging, 2) implement an opt-in tenant flag in Console/API and enable for small cohort for 2 weeks, 3) auto-opt-in for tenants that show >95% success and low parse_fail, 4) expand cohort gradually with a 2-week rollback guard, 5) publish a 90-day sunset notice after full enable.

Olivia: Security asks: redact any parsed content before logging, reject huge content-length early, add circuit-breaker per tenant so CPU/parse storms are cut off, and run fuzzing on the parser.

Sam: Runbook & alerts: create an incident playbook titled "compat edge shim fail" with steps to disable filter per cluster/tenant, remove rewrite, and global rollback. Also add dashboards for shard-level shim latency. I'll own alerts and dashboards.

Jordan: I'll implement the Envoy Lua with the prefix-limit and additive metrics. I'll include unit tests and a small load test to validate CPU cost.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: infra/edge-lua-shim v1 -> staging at 1718250000 :rocket:

Ava: Action items: Jordan implement shard-safe Lua w/ prefix limit and parse timeout; Sam add metrics, alerts, dashboard; Maria + Ken validate mobile SDKs and surface quick migration tips; Olivia write security checklist & fuzzing plan; I'll draft customer-facing deprecation copy and the 90-day notice. Sync tomorrow 10:00am to confirm staging results. :calendar:
